about: Material properties for stone strength and stone heat, from maker sheets that test printed specimens in the layer plane (X-Y) and across layers (Z). Strength and stiffness: stone uses the one sheet with the lowest Z strength and takes X-Y and Z from it, so the pair comes from one test series; range and others hold the other makers. Heat deflection: the lowest maker value. A value with an assumption field is a modeling choice, not a measurement.

entries.note: No DMA of printed PC found. Stone gives PC the shape of the three printed amorphous curves in this file (PETG, ABS, ASA), each read at the same distance from its own HDT at 0.45 MPa and averaged, placed on PC's HDT (111 C). PC keeps 0.27 at its HDT; the measured curves keep 0.47, 0.23 and 0.10 at theirs (PLA 0.62).
entries.quote: Figure 17. Storage and loss modulus of PETG-100-030-DMA samples. Figure 20. Storage and loss modulus of ABS-100-030-DMA samples. Figure 21. Storage and loss modulus of ASA-100-030-DMA samples.
entries.source: Mikula et al., Wear and Dynamic Mechanical Analysis (DMA) of Samples Produced via Fused Deposition Modelling (FDM) 3D Printing Method, Polymers 2024, 16(21), 3018
entries.assumption: Printed amorphous plastics lose stiffness on the same path measured from their HDT, so PC follows the mean of the PETG, ABS and ASA retention curves shifted to its HDT (points every 10 C, HDT - 80 to HDT + 20).

entries.source: Validation of Filament Materials for Injection Moulding 3D-Printed Inserts Using Temperature and Cavity Pressure, Materials 2026, 19(2), 369, section 3.1, after Takemori, Polym Eng Sci 1979 19:1104
entries.assumption: Stone warns of creep when the service temperature is within 20 C of the HDT under a lasting load; the 20 C margin is a rule of thumb, not a measured limit.
